title: Bowing and kneeling suit the present, not a Saint in America or China, still less one in heaven
source_text: XXXI. Sic viros sanctos quibuscum versamur officiose salutamus, caput illis aperimus, & corpus inclinamus: sed talibus honoris signis uti solemus tantum erga praesentes. Et absurdum esset, si quis in honorem hominis Sancti, apud Americanos, aut Sinenses peregrinantis, hic in Gallia domi suae, vel in loco sacro, corpus inclinaret, aut genua flecteret. Ideoque cum Sancti in caelo cum Christo regnantes tantum a nobis absint, quantum a terra caelum, a ratione putant omnino alienum esse, ut honoris ejusmodi signa erga illos adhibeamus.
pass_a_gloss: Thus we dutifully greet holy men with whom we live, we uncover the head to them, and we bow the body: but we are accustomed to use such signs of honor only toward those who are present. And it would be absurd if someone, in honor of a holy man traveling among the Americans or the Chinese, should here in France, at home or in a sacred place, bow the body or bend the knees. And therefore, since the Saints reigning in heaven with Christ are as far from us as heaven is from earth, they think it altogether alien to reason that we should use signs of honor of that sort toward them.
pass_b_english: Greeting, uncovering the head, and bowing are used toward holy people we actually live with, and only when they are present.
It would be absurd to bow or kneel in France, at home or in church, to honor a holy man traveling in the Americas or in China.
Saints reigning with Christ are as far from us as heaven from earth, so those signs toward them are held contrary to reason.

choices.why: The distance example is geographical absence, the step below heavenly absence.
rejected: the living in the same room
